note: Chapter 4 dialogue, Silver and Snow (Coldwater, the Kestrel mine, the Kestrel Pass, the line shack). id, speaker, line, emotion. Speaker voice fields name voice types from voices.json. Original writing.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Snow on the high ground already, and it isn't Thanksgiving. Whoever named Coldwater was an honest man.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You'd be the woman who put Cutter Shale in Mabry's jail. The whole canyon's heard. Half of it is buying you drinks you'll never collect.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You'd be the woman who left Cutter Shale on the Dry Fork. The whole canyon's heard. Nobody's sure whether to thank you or move away.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And you're the man reading a newspaper in a livery stable at nine in the morning.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Joseph Kehoe. I trade horses. Newspapers are the one thing in Coldwater nobody's charging double for.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Fenn printed your deeds, by the way. Every name. He spelled most of them right, which is more than the deeds did.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'm told Asa Shale is up here.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: With twenty company guards. Captain Ashby's men, hired to break the strike. The boy holds Ashby's horse, mostly. Old habits.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Why tell me?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Because you'll find out anyway, and I'd rather you found out from someone who'd like the miners left out of your business.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: Two dollars and a half a day, Mr. Garrity said. Then he made it two. Then he made it company scrip that only spends at his store.

lines.speaker: dai
lines.line: We go back when it's three dollars cash and timber in the drifts that isn't rotten through. Not one day before.

lines.speaker: ashby
lines.line: This assembly is on company ground. Disperse, or be dispersed. Your choice. I prefer the second; it's quicker.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's a public street, Captain. I asked. The company doesn't own the snow yet.

lines.speaker: ashby
lines.line: Not yet. Next quarter. Gentlemen, the lady is part of the assembly.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Not here. Not with women at the kettles. Watch who Ashby talks to after. That's where the trouble's kept.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: All right. I'll watch. I don't have to like it.

lines.speaker: garrity
lines.line: Thursday. The powder goes into number two drift. Nobody works number two on a Thursday.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Nobody's supposed to. Mr. Garrity, the strikers sometimes go in after their tools.

lines.speaker: garrity
lines.line: Then it's an accident, son. Mines are famous for them. Your brother understands accidents.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: That boy of Ashby's was asking the powder monkey about number two drift. Asking polite. Nobody up here asks polite.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Number two. Who goes in there?

lines.speaker: dai
lines.line: Nobody, since the strike. Only us, for our tools, when the guards are at dinner. Why?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You should stay at Nora's. The hotel belongs to Garrity, and so does the bed, and so does whoever's under it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You're very particular about where I sleep, Mr. Kehoe.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I'm particular about where people die. It's a habit. I'd like to lose it.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: There's soup. There's always soup. It's the one thing the company can't put in scrip.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Thursday. Dai said the guards eat at noon. It's ten to.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Dai and three men went into number two a quarter hour ago. Picks and a lantern. They didn't see me wave.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then we get them out before Garrity's accident gets them.

lines.speaker: hensley
lines.line: Fire in the hole, boys. And no, I didn't see nobody go in. Nobody saw me not see 'em.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Get down!

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: Dai! Dai's in there! Tommy Rees and the Morgan brothers! Somebody dig!

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: That's Hensley on the bay, riding for the company office. He lit it. If he gets there, it was never him.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Dig them out. Joseph, Nora, the timbers. Hensley can keep.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Joseph, dig. I'm going after Hensley. Somebody's going to answer for this with his own mouth.

lines.speaker: rees
lines.line: We hear you! We hear you! Dai's leg's pinned, and the air's going bad!

lines.speaker: dai
lines.line: I owe you a drink, missus. I owe you a barrel. I'll owe you till I'm dead, which isn't today, thanks to you.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: All four. All four of them, breathing. God bless every one of your blisters.

lines.speaker: hensley
lines.line: All right! All right! Garrity paid me six dollars! Six dollars and a bottle! I didn't know anybody was in there!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You said nobody saw you not see them. Say it again to a mine inspector.

lines.speaker: hensley
lines.line: You'll never prove it. Company's got lawyers like a dog's got fleas.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Three of them came out. Tommy Rees didn't. The timber came down on him while we were reaching for Dai.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: Tommy had a girl in Cardiff he was saving to send for. Eleven years saving. I'll have to write her.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I chose the man on the horse. Tommy paid for it.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Somebody always pays, Mrs. Caddell. The trick is not to make it a habit of choosing who.

lines.speaker: garrity
lines.line: A tragic accident. The company will pay for the funeral. In scrip, naturally, redeemable at the store.

lines.speaker: dai
lines.line: You'll pay in something, Garrity. Not scrip.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Asa Shale lit out an hour ago, over the Kestrel Pass, with a letter in his coat for his brother. I watched him saddle.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Over the pass. In this?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: The Shales don't wait for weather. Neither do I. I know a way up the face that comes out ahead of him.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You've decided this is your fight now?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I've decided I don't want to read about it in the paper.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: The trail goes round by the switchbacks. We go straight up. Hands, feet, and don't look at the view. The view doesn't care about you.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I used to do this sort of thing for money. Ladders, mostly. With a band playing.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: There's no band up here. Only wind. It plays one tune and it's very sure of it.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Your hands are white. There's a herder's shack halfway. Get to the fire before you lose fingers you'll want later.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Tom used to put my hands in his coat when the show played winter towns. Inside, against his shirt. I haven't been warm like that since.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: There. The pass. And there's Asa's string, coming up the far switchback. Three riders and a pack mule.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: It's her! The Caddell woman! Shoot! Shoot, damn you!

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: No! Not on this slope! Not with the cornice hanging over!

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Slide! Run for the rocks! Left, Ruth, left!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Joseph! Joseph, where are you?

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Here. Under about a ton of winter. My leg's in a direction I don't approve of.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hold still. I'm digging. Talk to me while I dig.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Go. His tracks won't last an hour in this wind. I'll dig myself out. I've done it before.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: About the newspapers. I read them because I like knowing what people believe happened. It's never what did.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: There. Arm round my neck. You're heavier than you look.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Everyone is, in the snow.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You came back. I'd have bet against it. I'd have lost, and I'd have been glad.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: His tracks went east. Toward the line shack under the ridge.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: The line shack. Two men left with him and the mule. He'll hole up till the storm breaks. So will we, or we'll freeze arguing about it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll go now. While the trail's warm.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Then go. I'll catch you up limping. I'm good at limping. Had practice.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I left you in the snow.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You left me with a shovel. There's a difference. Not a large one.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Hands to the fire, not in it. You've the look of a woman who'd do either.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've been colder. I can't remember when, but I'm sure I have.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Smoke from the chimney, three horses in the lean-to, and a mule that's given up on all of them.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Two rifles at the window. The boy's the one by the door, pretending he isn't scared. He isn't good at it.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Stay back! I got a rifle and I got a letter for my brother and I ain't giving up neither one!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Asa. Send your friends out with their hands up and nobody else has to be in the snow tonight.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: You killed my brother! Or you put him in a cage, which is worse for Cutter. He always said he'd rather be shot.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Here they come. They've decided for him.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Don't. Please. My leg's done. I just held the horses. At the Siding. I just held the horses, I swear on Eben's Bible.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You held the horses while your brothers shot my husband in the door of the car. What did you do after?

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: I threw up. Eben laughed. He said it gets easier. It never did. I don't think he wanted it to, for me.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: There's a letter in his coat. Garrity's hand. Thursday's powder and who paid for it. That's worth more than the boy is.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Give me the letter, Asa.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Take it. Take it. Eben will know I gave it up. He'll know.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Go west, Asa. California. Change your name, and if I ever hear the old one again, I'll know where to find it.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Why? Why would you?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Because you were nineteen, and holding the horses, and I'd like one of you Shales to find out what that's worth.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You held the horses. Somebody always holds the horses. That's how the rest of it gets done.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I've stood in a place where men shot boys because they were close enough to shoot. I don't talk about it. I won't talk about this either.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: That was well done. It was harder than the other thing. Most good things are.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I'll ride with you as far as Eben. After that we'll see whose fight it is.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That's further than most people offer.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Most people haven't read the papers.

lines.speaker: asa
lines.line: Tell Eben... no. Don't tell Eben anything. I'll tell him myself someday, from a long way off.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Joseph. Don't look at me like that.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I'm not looking at you. I'm looking at the snow. It covers things. That's all it's good for.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Joseph, take the left. Keep them at the window. I'm going round by the woodpile.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: Ashby's men are coming down the hill with torches. They mean to burn the kitchen and call it a stove fire.

lines.speaker: dai
lines.line: Then we'll be at the kitchen. All of us. The ones with rifles in front.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Keep the women behind the wagons. Joseph, the roof. Nobody gets a torch to that door.

lines.speaker: ashby
lines.line: Last chance, Kilbride! Go back to work, or go back to Wales!

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: I'm from Galway, you ignorant man! And I'm not going anywhere!

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: The kitchen stands. Soup for everyone. Even the Captain, if he'd stopped to ask.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: They got the roof. The kettles are fine. We'll cook in the snow. We've done it before.

lines.speaker: garrity
lines.line: Mrs. Caddell. Let's be reasonable people. I'm a superintendent. I follow instructions. The instructions come from Port Linden.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then here's an instruction. Three dollars cash, timbered drifts, and Tommy Rees's girl in Cardiff gets his wages till she marries.

lines.speaker: garrity
lines.line: I can't sign that. Mr. Pell would have my position.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Mr. Pell isn't holding the pen. Sign it, Mr. Garrity. My hand's steadier than yours, and it's not holding a pen either.

lines.speaker: garrity
lines.line: Signed. You know it won't hold. A contract at gunpoint is waste paper in any court in the territory.

lines.speaker: dai
lines.line: It'll hold till spring. Spring's further than we've seen in a while.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No. You'll answer to the territorial inspector, with Garrity's own letter and Hensley's six dollars. Paper against paper, Mr. Garrity.

lines.speaker: inspector
lines.line: Powder in a drift with men in it, and the superintendent's hand on the order. I've been inspecting mines twenty years. This is a new low, and I'd thought I'd seen the floor.

lines.speaker: garrity
lines.line: You'll be in Port Linden by Christmas and I'll be back by New Year's. Mr. Pell doesn't lose people. He mislays them for a while.

lines.speaker: nora
lines.line: It'll be slow, the law's way. But it's ours, and it's in writing, and nobody had to hold a gun to get it.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: I've a string of horses to sell before the pass closes for good. And then I've a camp to find. Willow Bend, I hear.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: There's a drover who sings hymns badly, a doctor who reads Latin to the horses, a cardsharp and a boy. There's room.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: A doctor who reads Latin to horses. I'll bring newspapers. Somebody should read them English.

lines.speaker: hap
lines.line: Another one! Del, set a plate. He looks like a man who's been eating snow.

lines.speaker: del
lines.line: Mr. Kehoe. Do you play cards? Don't answer. Everybody lies about that the first night.

lines.speaker: doc
lines.line: A scout. Splendid. Someone to tell us which way we're running.

lines.speaker: billy
lines.line: Is that a Lakota saddle? Can I see it? Can I sit on it? I won't, I just want to know if I could.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: You can sit on it, Billy. If you can tell me which of my horses is lame.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Three names done, one way or another. One left. And he's the one who reads a Bible over the men he kills.

lines.speaker: joseph
lines.line: Then we'll need to know what chapter he's on.
